title: Trash
hint: Deleted sessions and projects stay here until you delete them permanently. Nothing is removed from disk before that.
remote: Deleting permanently is only possible on the machine itself. From a remote desktop you can restore.

empty.title: The Trash is empty
empty.hint: Sessions and projects you delete land here, and can be restored until you delete them permanently.

confirm.purgeSessionMessage: Delete "{label}" permanently? {count} session will be lost, with its log and transcript. This cannot be undone. | Delete "{label}" permanently? {count} sessions (it and its workers) will be lost, with their logs and transcripts. This cannot be undone.
confirm.purgeProjectMessage: Delete project "{name}" permanently? {count} session will be lost. This cannot be undone. | Delete project "{name}" permanently? {count} sessions will be lost. This cannot be undone.
confirm.purgeGroupMessage: Delete the sessions of "{name}" in the Trash permanently? {count} session will be lost, with its log and transcript. confirm.emptyMessage: Delete everything in the Trash permanently? {sessions} and {projects} will be lost. This cannot be undone.
confirm.restoreWithProjectMessage: Project "{name}" is in the Trash too. Restoring this session restores the project as well, with its sessions that were not deleted on their own.
confirm.purgeMatchedMessage: Delete {count} session matching “{query}” in "{name}" permanently? {remaining} other sessions of the project stay in the Trash. confirm.restoreMatchedMessage: Project "{name}" is in the Trash too. Restoring {count} matching sessions restores the project as well, with {others} other sessions that are in the Trash only because of the project.
